title: Bioavailability and Metabolic Pharmacokinetics of Rutin and Quercetin ...
abstract:
The document is a research paper titled "Bioavailability and Metabolic Pharmacokinetics of Rutin and Quercetin in Rats". It is a 16-page PDF file of 1020Kb. The paper was received on May 9, 2005, and accepted on June 8, 2005.

The study aimed to characterize and compare the bioavailability and metabolic pharmacokinetics of rutin and quercetin in rats. Quercetin was administered intravenously (33 µmol/kg) and orally (165 µmol/kg), while rutin was administered only orally (328 µmol/kg). Blood samples were analyzed using HPLC to determine the concentrations of quercetin before and after hydrolysis.

Key findings include:
- After intravenous administration of quercetin, 93.8% of the dose circulated as its sulfates and glucuronides.
- After oral administration of quercetin, only glucuronides and sulfates of quercetin were detected in the bloodstream, with no parent quercetin. The oral absorption rate of quercetin was 53% compared to intravenous administration after dose correction.
- When rutin was orally administered, only sulfates and glucuronides of quercetin were found in the bloodstream, with neither rutin nor quercetin detected in their parent forms.
- Quercetin showed a higher oral absorption rate than rutin.
- The study concluded that quercetin sulfates and quercetin glucuronides are the major metabolites when either rutin or quercetin is administered to rats.

The paper lists the authors as CHI-YU YANG, SU-LAN HSIU, KUO-CHING WEN, SHIUAN-PEY LIN, SHANG-YUAN TSAI, YU-CHI HOU, and PEI-DAWN LEE CHAO, affiliated with China Medical University in Taichung, Taiwan, R.O.C.
